title: Annotatio V §.IV §.6: Author §14 — denying Supper-article fundamentality contradicts self, companions, Scripture
pass_a_gloss: §. 6. Meanwhile, that he might reproach me worthily enough and sensibly for the Fundamentalitatem of the Oral Eating of Christ’s Body denied by me as concerns the Christian Faith, the Famous Author argues in §. 14 that by denying the Article on the Sacred Supper to be fundamental I have contradicted myself, and my faith’s Companions, and Sacred Scripture (which GOD forbid), and the whole Analogy of faith. Myself indeed, while at p. 73 I had held every and only Article in Sacred Scripture said necessary to salvation — either in express words or by evident Consequence — to be Fundamental; And yet in the Article on the Supper (perhaps even as to the Oral Eating of Christ’s Body) this kind of necessity shows itself manifest — namely both of mandate, when it is said: Do this in remembrance of me; and of means, seeing Christ’s Body was given for us.
pass_b_english: §.IV §.6: Author §.14 reproaches Strimesius for denying Oral’s Fundamentalitatem — claiming contradiction of self, faith-companions, Scripture, and the analogy of faith.
The charge turns on Strimesius’s own rule (p. 73): only Scripture-necessary articles are fundamental — and the Author says the Supper shows mandate (‘do this’) and means (body given for us).
source_text: §. 6. Interim quò denegatam à me, Orali Manducationis Corporis Christi, Fundamentalitatem, quòd ad Fidem Christianam attinet, dignè satis ac sensibiliter exprobraret mihi, arguit Clar. Autor §. 14. me negando Articulum de S. Cœna, fundamentalem esse, & mihi ipsi, & Sociis fidei meæ, & Scripturæ S. (quod DEUS prohibeat,) totique Analogiæ fidei contradixisse. Mihi quidem ipsi, dum omnem solumque Articulum in Scriptura S. ad salutem, vel conceptis verbis, vel per evidentem Consequentiam necessarium dictum p. 73. perhibuerim Fundamentalem esse; Atqui in Articulo de Cœna (fortean etiam quoad Oralem Corporis Christi Manducationem) hujusmodi necessitas se prodat manifesta, scil. tam mandati, quando dicitur: Hoc facite in mei commemorationem: quàm medii, siquidem Corpus Christi pro nobis datum.
